speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and having a distended belly; can you tell me if you are vomiting, and if so, is it coming up undigested food or just milk?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. The tenderness when touching the belly is concerning. Have you noticed any "currant jelly" colored stools, or has your baby been passing gas or having bowel movements? Also, is the vomiting forceful and projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever, projectile vomiting, or diarrhea are present, and the baby had an uncomplicated birth. Have you noticed any red, currant-jelly stools, or is the abdomen tender and distended to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
You mentioned the baby hasn't passed stool normally and the abdomen is increasingly distended. Can you tell me if the baby has been passing any gas, and is there visible, red streaking in the diaper? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception
